units.title: Plants, Animals and the Environment
units.intro:
**Adaptation** is a feature that helps survival and reproduction in a habitat. Not “the animal wanted it.”

**Plants:** cold — short season, dwarf, dark leaves sometimes. Drought — small/waxy leaves, sunken stomata, deep or wide roots, water store (cactus). Salt — salt glands, succulence. Wind — flexible stems, small leaves. Eritrea highland vs coastal desert is the local pair to use in essays.

cards.title: 4.1 What is Adaptation?
body: Living organisms are characterized by the changes they make to live in the environmental conditions around them.
The changes can be morphological (change in structure and form) or physiological (internal and functional change), and is called **adaptation**.
**Adaptation** is the modification in structure or function that increases the fitness of an organism in a stressful environment.
Adaptation is hereditary and thus passed from one generation to the next.
Adaptation mechanisms of living organisms to various environmental stress factors are generally classified as avoidance, tolerance and escape mechanisms.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: Which of the following terms describes the hereditary modification of an organism's structure, behavior, or function that increases its chance of survival and reproduction in a specific habitat?

steps.text: **Step 1: Define the biological terms in the options**
*   Metabolism refers to all chemical reactions inside cells.
*   Homeostasis is the maintenance of a constant internal environment.
*   Adaptation is the hereditary modification in structure, function, or behavior that increases an organism's fitness.
*   Metamorphosis is a developmental change in body form.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: Plants that are adapted to grow under normal water conditions or intermediate water availability are known as:

steps.text: **Step 1: Classify plants by water adaptation**
*   Xerophytes: adapted to dry habitats (water scarcity).
*   Hydrophytes: adapted to wet or aquatic habitats (excess water).
*   Mesophytes: adapted to moderate land habitats (intermediate water).
*   Halophytes: adapted to highly saline/salty soils.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following is a physical adaptation of xerophytes specifically designed to reduce water loss from transpiration?

options.A: Large air chambers inside leaves and stems
options.B: Broad, flat leaves with stomata on the upper surface
options.D: Lack of a waxy cuticle layer

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze adaptations of xerophytes**
Xerophytes must reduce transpiration (water loss). Having leaves modified into sharp spines reduces the leaf surface area exposed to the sun and wind, thus drastically minimizing water loss.

**Final Result:**
**Leaves modified into sharp spines**.

**Step 2: Match with classification**
Plants adapted to aquatic environments are called hydrophytes.

**Final Result:**
**Hydrophytes**.

lessons.title: Adaptations of Plants to their Environment

cards.title: 4.2.1 Adaptations of Plants to Temperature
body: **Temperature** is a very important environmental factor that affects plant functions and growth.
At low temperatures, plants develop adaptations that allow them to reduce their exposure to the cold environment.
**Transpiration** is the loss of water from plants through the small openings called stomata in the leaves and stems.
The low temperature limits soil water uptake.

cards.title: 4.2.2 Adaptations of Plants to Water
body: Plants are classified into three major categories according to their adaptations to water conditions.
The majority of plant species live in optimal environments with regard to water availability.
Mesophytes are plants that live under normal water conditions or in intermediate water availability e.g. many crop species.
Mesophytes usually have a well developed root system, their leaves are flat and their stomata do not have protective features.

cards.title: 4.2.3 Adaptations of Plants to Salt
body: Plants such as mangroves, that cover a great part of the seashores in Massawa and the coastal areas, are salt-tolerant plants.
Mangroves also have small openings (lenticels) in their bark that allow oxygen to diffuse into the plant and down into its underground roots.
Many salt-tolerant plants have developed salt glands, salt-filtering root, or salt-excreting leaves or branches in order to prevent the build up of high salt concentrations.
Mangroves for example almost completely eliminate salt and, when squeezed, their leaves consist of almost pure water.

cards.title: 4.2.4 Adaptations of Plants to Air

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Rhizomes are plant parts produced as a response to
cards.why: Rhizomes are underground stems that store food and water. Many plants produce them as an adaptation to survive unfavorable conditions like a **dry season**. During drought, the above-ground parts may die, but the rhizome remains dormant underground and regrows when rain returns.

lessons.title: Adaptations of Animals to their Environment

cards.title: Adaptations of Animals to their Environment
body: **Animals:** cold — fur, fat, shiver, migrate, hibernate, small ears. Heat — thin fur, large ears, nocturnal, panting, pale colour, burrow. Always pair the feature with the job.

cards.title: Feature → function → habitat
body: Never list spikes without “to cut water loss in a dry place.” Three-part sentence scores.

cards.title: 4.3.1 Adaptations of Animals to Low Temperatures
body: The ear size of goats living in cold regions is smaller than that of goats living in warm regions.
Hormonal changes: In cold weather hormonal changes tend to boost the metabolic rate.
Insulation: A major thermoregulatory adaptation in mammals and birds is insulation.
Mammals develop hair (often called fur), or have fat deposits in their bodies.

cards.title: 4.3.2 Adaptations of Animals to High Temperatures
body: Aestivation: In regions where the day-time temperature is very high and the water supply is very scarce, some animals tolerate (endure) the period of high temperature by aestivation.
Nocturnal behaviour: There are many animals that become active and feed during the night, becoming inactive during the day e.g. bats.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: An air plant, such as an orchid, that grows upon another plant for physical support but does not extract nutrients or water from its host is called a/an:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the relationship described**
*   Grows on another plant solely for support/height (not parasitic).
*   Obtains its own moisture from rain and air.

**Step 2: Match with the definition**
This is the definition of an epiphyte (air plant).

**Final Result:**
**Epiphyte**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the name of the thick, waxy outer layer on the leaves and stems of land plants that functions to reduce water loss from evaporation?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Define the structural layers of a leaf**
*   Stomata: breathing pores.
*   Epidermis: outermost cell layer.
*   Aerenchyma: air-storing tissue in water plants.
*   Cuticle: waxy, waterproof non-cellular outer layer that minimizes water loss.

**Final Result:**
**Cuticle**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: All of the following are true about adaptation of animals to **high temperature**, **except**
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Analyze heat adaptations. Aestivation (summer sleep), nocturnal activity, lack of insulating fat, and large ears (for cooling) are all heat adaptations.
**Step 2:** **Hibernation** (winter sleep) is a state of inactivity and metabolic depression in endotherms to survive cold temperatures and food scarcity.
**Step 3:** Therefore, hibernation is not an adaptation to high temperature.

tips.text: Plants are classified into mesophytes, hydrophytes and xerophytes, according to the adaptations they have developed in response to water conditions.
They also show various adaptation mechanisms such as leaf rolling, leaf shedding, the presence of a cuticle, and modified leaves, roots and other plant parts in response to different temperatures.

For example the polar bear’s thick fur gives it warmth in cold temperatures.
